facts.label: official
facts.quote: As a result, taxpayers will be required to pay a fee of Rs. 500 up to three months from 1st April, 2022 and a fee of Rs.1000 after that, while intimating their Aadhaar.
facts.text: Taxpayers who missed the deadline to link their PAN with Aadhaar must pay a late fee of 1,000 INR to complete the linking.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: permanent account number shall become operative within thirty days from the date of intimation of Aadhaar number.
facts.text: An inoperative PAN is restored to operative status within 30 days after the taxpayer intimates their Aadhaar and pays the fee.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: It is stated that more than 51 crore PANs have already been linked with Aadhaar till date.
facts.text: Over 51 crore PAN cards had been successfully linked with Aadhaar before the statutory inoperative deadline took effect.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Section 139AA of the Income Tax Act provides that every individual who has been allotted a permanent account number (PAN) as on the 1st day of July, 2017, and who is eligible to obtain an Aadhaar number, shall intimate his Aadhaar number in the prescribed form and manner.
facts.text: Mandatory PAN-Aadhaar linkage applies to all eligible individuals who received their PAN on or before 1 July 2017.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Aadhaar-PAN linkage requirement does not apply to any individual who is: Residing in the States of Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, and Meghalaya;; a non-resident as per the Income-tax Act, 1961;; of the age of eighty years or more at any time during the previous year; or; not a citizen of India.
facts.text: Individuals aged 80 years or older are explicitly exempt from the mandatory PAN-Aadhaar linking requirement.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Apart from this, if the person furnishes the PAN Card, which is no more valid, then under Section 272B of the Income Tax Act 1961, the Assessing Officer may direct that such person shall pay, by way of penalty, a sum of ₹10,000.
facts.text: Furnishing an invalid or inoperative PAN card can attract a penalty of 10,000 INR under Section 272B of the Income Tax Act.
